messages.content:
Validate the following vignette.

Patient demographics:
  age: 18
  gender: Male
  ethnicity: South Eastern Asian
  relationship_status: Single
  occupation: Photographer
  trauma_type: Combat
  pcl5: 77

Patient-reported symptoms:
  Threat: Risky Behavior: Taking too many risks or doing things that could cause you harm, Cannot Relax: I am unable to relax even when I know I am in a safe place, Startle to Sounds: I jump or startle at ordinary sounds that would not bother most people
  Memory: More Real Than Normal: My memories of the event feel more real and vivid than memories of ordinary things, Rage on Recall: When I remember the event I feel intense rage, Triggered Without Warning: Something in my surroundings can instantly bring back the full memory without warning
  Negative Appraisals: Belong Nowhere: I no longer belong anywhere, Mistrust: People can't be trusted, Failed to Protect: I should have protected others and I failed

Vignette:
Meet Rajiv, an 18-year-old South Eastern Asian male who has recently returned from a brief stint in the military. He is currently working as a photographer but finds it increasingly difficult to focus on his work due to persistent symptoms of post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) following his combat experiences. Rajiv was deployed to a volatile region where he witnessed intense and traumatic events, including direct combat and the loss of comrades. One particularly harrowing incident involved an ambush in which Rajiv saw fellow soldiers injured and killed before his eyes. The sound of gunfire and explosions became etched into his memory, making ordinary noises like car horns or fireworks unbearable triggers for him. Since returning home, Rajiv has found himself struggling to relax even when he knows he is safe. He often takes unnecessary risks by driving aggressively or hiking alone in dangerous areas. These behaviors stem from a deep-seated feeling that nothing can truly be trusted, leading him to seek constant adrenaline rushes and distractions from his intrusive thoughts. The vividness of his combat memories makes them feel more real than any other experience he has had. Flashbacks are frequent and can be triggered without warning by mundane sights or sounds. When Rajiv remembers the event, intense rage surges through him, leaving him feeling helpless and angry at himself for not having done enough to protect others. Rajiv's mistrust of people is profound; he believes that no one can truly be trusted after what he has seen in combat. This belief has led to a significant withdrawal from social interactions. He often isolates himself and avoids public places, finding it nearly impossible to engage with his colleagues or friends without feeling on edge. His occupation as a photographer has also been severely impacted by these symptoms. When Rajiv is out taking photos, the sound of a sudden noise can immediately trigger memories that leave him shaken and unable to continue his work for hours. This has resulted in missed assignments and strained relationships with clients who expect reliable service from him. Rajiv's sense of dislocation is palpable; he feels as though he no longer belongs anywhere. He struggles to connect with others because of the deep mistrust that has developed since returning home, and he often thinks about how his failure to protect others during combat haunts him constantly. This feeling of guilt and inadequacy adds to his distress, making it difficult for him to function in his daily life. What finally prompted Rajiv to seek help was a particularly intense flashback while out on assignment that left him paralyzed with rage and unable to complete the job. He realized that his symptoms were not only affecting his work but also his ability to maintain any semblance of normalcy in his life. Rajiv is most afraid of losing control and feeling like he no longer belongs anywhere, but he hopes for a chance to regain some stability and peace within himself. He seeks help with the hope of understanding why these memories continue to haunt him so vividly and how he can navigate his daily life without being constantly on guard.
